q: The structural chain of an Indian mutual fund is:
e: Sponsor establishes the Trust; Trustees safeguard investor interest and appoint the AMC; AMC manages day-to-day operations. Custodian holds securities; RTA maintains records.

q: Minimum number of trustees required for an Indian mutual fund is:
e: Minimum 4 trustees, with at least 2/3 being independent (not connected to the Sponsor). Trustees act in fiduciary capacity for investors.

q: The Sponsor must contribute at least what proportion of the AMC's net worth?
e: Sponsor must contribute at least 40% of the AMC's net worth — ensures meaningful skin-in-the-game. Less than 40% disqualifies the sponsor relationship.

q: Minimum net worth required for an AMC is:
e: AMC minimum net worth is ₹50 crore (NOT ₹50 lakh — common decimal trap). Net worth must be maintained continuously; falling below triggers regulatory action.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the typical roles in MF operations?
e: Custodian, RTA, and AMC's Auditor are typical service providers. A stock-exchange clearing member is involved when MFs trade — but it's not a structural role of the MF itself.

q: AMC must contribute to every scheme it launches at least:
o: 1% of the amount raised, subject to a maximum of ₹50 lakh
e: AMC (or its associates) must contribute at least 1% of the amount raised in the scheme, subject to a maximum cap of ₹50 lakh. Ensures AMC has skin-in-the-game per scheme.
